scenario: Registrar account takeover unlocks or repoints the firm's domain, redirecting web and mail traffic to an attacker
threat_source: External attacker using phished or reused administrator credentials
affected_assets: Registered domains; DNS zones; inbound mail; public website; investor trust
treatment: Keep transfer lock and auto-renew on; enforce 2FA and least-privilege membership; alert on unlock, contact, and nameserver changes in the audit log; rehearse registrar recovery

scenario: An unreviewed DNS record change points a hostname at the wrong destination or breaks mail authentication for the firm's domain
threat_source: Insider error or a compromised account member
affected_assets: DNS zones; mail flow; SaaS verification records; public website
treatment: Document record owners with comments or tags; keep a dated zone export; review DNS changes in the audit log; require a second person for production record changes

scenario: An over-scoped, non-expiring API token used by an automation is leaked from a repository or log and used to alter zones or security settings
threat_source: External attacker with access to leaked secrets; departed contractor
affected_assets: DNS zones; WAF and TLS settings; Access policies; account audit trail
treatment: Issue account-owned tokens with minimum permissions, zone scope, expiry, and client IP restriction; retire Global API Key use; roll tokens on leaver events; alert on token creation

scenario: The origin server is reachable directly by IP, so requests bypass the WAF, rate limiting, and Access entirely
threat_source: External attacker using historical DNS or certificate transparency data
affected_assets: Origin servers; application data; availability of the public website
treatment: Connect origins through Cloudflare Tunnel or enforce authenticated origin pulls with a Cloudflare IP allowlist; rotate origin IPs after onboarding; test direct-to-origin access each quarter

scenario: A web application vulnerability is exploited because managed rulesets are absent, log-only, or bypassed by a DNS-only record
threat_source: External attacker scanning for known vulnerabilities
affected_assets: Public website; content management system; visitor data
treatment: Deploy the managed rulesets available on the plan in blocking mode after a logged evaluation; proxy every hostname that carries an application; review security events weekly

scenario: Credential stuffing or brute force against a login or administrative path on a proxied hostname leads to account compromise or service degradation
affected_assets: Administrative interfaces; user accounts; application availability
treatment: Restrict administrative paths with Zone Lockdown or Access; enable the plan's bot protection; add rate limiting rules on login and form endpoints tested against legitimate clients

scenario: Mail is spoofed from a firm domain, including a parked domain, because SPF, DKIM, or DMARC records are missing or misaligned
threat_source: Phishing actor impersonating the firm to investors or portfolio companies
affected_assets: Firm reputation; investor and counterparty relationships; mail deliverability
treatment: Publish provider-documented SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records for every domain including non-sending ones; review DMARC reports; move to an enforcing DMARC policy after remediation

scenario: Visitor traffic is downgraded or intercepted through legacy TLS, or an expired origin certificate causes a 526 outage for the public website
treatment: Set minimum TLS 1.2, enable HSTS after subdomain review, use Full (strict) with tracked origin certificate expiry, and route certificate notifications to a monitored destination

scenario: A leaver retains access to an internal application because an Access policy references a stale group or email, or a One-time PIN login remains available
threat_source: Former staff member or contractor; attacker with the leaver's mailbox
affected_assets: Internal applications; deal and finance data; audit trail
treatment: Scope Access policies to identity provider groups; disable One-time PIN for staff applications; run the policy tester for each leaver; release the seat and verify denial

scenario: An unmanaged or compromised staff device reaches internal applications or resolves a phishing domain because posture checks and Gateway filtering are absent
threat_source: Malware on a personal device; phishing campaign
affected_assets: Internal applications; staff credentials; deal and finance data
treatment: Deploy the WARP client with approved posture checks; require posture in Access policies; block security categories in Gateway DNS; test a non-compliant device and a synthetic blocked lookup

scenario: The firm loses access to its Cloudflare account during an incident because the only super administrator has left or lost the 2FA device and backup codes
threat_source: Operational dependency on one person; lost or replaced hardware
affected_assets: Ability to change DNS, WAF, and Access settings under time pressure
treatment: Maintain at least two separately accountable super administrators with tested backup codes in private custody; rehearse the lockout and compromise-response steps; keep configuration exports outside the account

scenario: A security event or certificate failure goes unnoticed because notifications route to a departed person's mailbox and audit logs are never reviewed
affected_assets: Incident detection and response; log retention; public website availability
treatment: Route notifications to a shared, monitored destination with an owner; test delivery; review audit logs on a cadence; decide retention or export before the 18-month window expires
